title: Meerkats workflows_and_automations v1 — standing alert + workflow + standing-config lifecycle
description: The agentic standing-process family. alert is standing and READ-ONLY: it never mutates and never needs approval; delivery is slack or email ONLY (notify_channel). workflow is standing and WRITE: the only autonomous mutator — each step mutates through the SAME selection_request + operation vocabulary as a standalone action. DETERMINISM CONTRACT: the agent emits operations, never tools — the server-side binder resolves each step to an exact tool chain from the capability registry (capability-registry/v1) at CONFIG CREATION (tool_binding); no binding => fail closed at creation. APPROVAL CONTRACT: a workflow standing_config cannot be registered without approval_ref, and a workflow_run cannot exist without approval_ref — approved first, act second, structurally. Server-produced artifacts: standing_config (audit config_* target), tool_binding, workflow_run (idempotency keys + per-call verify + rollback), alert_firing (alerts never enter the audit log — this is their record). Cross-file $refs point at https://meerkats.ai/schemas/query_and_act/v1.json — both must be registered in the validator.

evaluate_every.description: How often a standing condition is re-evaluated. Server may clamp to platform sync cadence — evaluating faster than data lands only re-reads the same numbers.

notify_channel.description: Alert delivery surface. slack and email are the ONLY channels. Delivery tools + retry/fallback live in the capability registry (notify.slack_post falls back to notify.email_send).

channel.description: Slack channel id or #name the workspace's bot posts to (chat.postMessage)

alert_task.description: Standing, read-only. Never mutates, never needs approval. condition reuses metric_predicate — the same vocabulary a query's having clause speaks.

conditions.description: ANDed, same style as where/having — the alert fires when ALL hold (e.g. creative fatigue: frequency > 3 AND ctr_7d_change_pct < -20). Baseline-relative triggers stay plain predicates over DERIVED metrics the semantic layer mints (spend_dod_change_pct, hours_to_zero — contracts/config/primitives.yaml derived_alert_metrics); the schema never grows comparison logic.

trigger.description: What starts a workflow run: a schedule, or a named platform/system event.

workflow_step.description: A mutating step. select resolves to a fresh snapshot at run time; operation executes against it under the same on_drift/approval rules as a standalone action. The step carries a selection_request, never a resolved_selection — freezing happens per run, server-side.

workflow_task.description: Standing, WRITE. The only autonomous mutator. Every run is audited with actor.kind=workflow and on_behalf_of naming the human who approved the config — that pairing is what makes an unattended mutation non-repudiable (audit-log/v1).

standing_config.description: SERVER-PRODUCED registration of a standing task. This is what the audit log's config_created/updated/paused/deleted actions point at (subject.config_ref = config_id). The embedded task is immutable per version: config_updated writes a new version_seq, and the audit chain holds the history — a running workflow always cites the exact version it ran under.

task.description: the standing definition as validated at creation time

created_by.description: principal_ref of the human who created it; becomes actor.on_behalf_of in audit events for autonomous runs

approval_ref.description: audit event_id of the approval that authorized a WORKFLOW config (mutating configs require approval per policy; alert configs don't)

allOf.description: a WORKFLOW config mutates unattended — it cannot be registered without the approval that authorizes it, and without its tool binding (which is where an unbindable operation, e.g. any campaign.* on flipkart, fails closed at creation).

tool_binding.description: SERVER-PRODUCED at config creation. The BINDER resolves each step's (platform, entity, operation) through the capability registry's operation_bindings into an exact ordered tool chain — the agent never sees the registry and never chooses a tool. A step with no binding rejects the config at creation time (fail closed), never at run time.

registry_version.description: capability-registry meta.version the binding was resolved against

operation_key.description: the registry binding key used, e.g. campaign.pause

tool_chain.description: ordered tool_ids; reads may precede the mutation (increase_budget = read -> compute -> set)

workflow_run.description: SERVER-PRODUCED record of one workflow execution. approval_ref is REQUIRED — structurally, an unapproved run cannot exist: it cites the standing approval on the config (within validity) or the run-level re-approval after drift (on_drift=re_approve). Every mutating tool call carries an idempotency_key and is followed by its verify read; verify failure triggers the registry's rollback_tool if reversible, else escalation. Each mutating step is also audited (audit-log/v1, actor.kind=workflow).

config_version_seq.description: the exact config version this run executed

approval_ref.description: audit event_id of the approval_granted that authorizes this run

trigger_fired.description: schedule tick or event name that started the run

selection_ref.description: the resolved_selection frozen for THIS run (selection resolves fresh per run, server-side)

tool_id.description: from the config's tool_binding — never chosen at run time

idempotency_key.description: config_id:run_id:step:member — mandatory on mutating calls; a retry can never double-apply

alert_firing.description: SERVER-PRODUCED record of one alert trigger. Alerts are read-only, so they never enter the audit log (audit is scoped to mutation) — this artifact, cited from the task-trace, is their record. It also encodes the never-bare contract: a firing carries the observed values AND the prefilled drill-down query the notification lands on.

conditions.description: echo of the config's conditions as evaluated at fire time

observed.description: what the evaluation actually saw — the evidence behind the firing

drill_down.description: the prefilled query the notification links to — an alert is never bare

delivery_status.description: slack failure retries then falls back to email (registry notify.slack_post.delivery); failed surfaces in-app

dedupe_key.description: same key within cooldown => suppressed duplicate, no second notification

suppressed_reason.description: set when the firing was withheld, e.g. sync_staleness_active (never alert on stale data as if current) or partial_scrape_run
